---

title: "Research"

---

\## Climate Extremes and Forest Growth

I investigate how the timing, duration, and persistence of extreme heat and elevated vapor pressure deficit influence woody growth in eastern U.S. temperate forests.

Using long-term ForestGEO observations and high-frequency dendrometer measurements, I examine how forest growth responds to environmental stress within and across growing seasons.

\## Carbon Uptake and Woody Biomass Accumulation

A central focus of my research is understanding when canopy carbon uptake and woody growth diverge under climate stress.

I integrate tree-growth observations, flux-tower measurements, and remote sensing to investigate whether photosynthetic carbon uptake reliably translates into long-lived woody biomass.

\## Forest Disturbance and Structural Damage

I also examine how non-lethal crown damage affects individual tree growth and stand-level aboveground woody productivity.

This research draws on long-term monitoring at the Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute's ForestGEO forest dynamics plot.
